warnings: Steel hip-roof framing ('โครงหลังคา ดูแบบขยาย' — truss details on S-22 / S-23). Common trusses T1 are drawn at three equal spaces per 4.00 bay (~1.33) from 5.33 to 74.67 — 53 trusses, each one prefabricated member recorded eave-to-eave (A'' to D'''''), like house 165. S-06 does not dimension the spacing: 17 trusses sit on grid lines; the 36 in between were placed at thirds of each bay by proportion, and the alternative prefab truss plan PT-02 (page 59) prints exactly those thirds (1.33), so the lines are printed ticks in the grid master. span_source is grid_table because the span (eave to eave) is read from the y lines. The printed 0.08 (hip apex to the first T1) confirms 5.33 - 5.25.

Hip ends (bays 1-2 and 20-21): T3 along the hips, jack trusses T4-T6 (S-23: each frames into T3) and T7 (= C-100x50x20x2.3mm). T2 on grids 2 / 20 is a full eave-to-eave truss (S-22 elevation: 2.20 + 10.50 + 2.20), carrying the hip trusses T3 / T4 at 3.94 from each support (S-22). T3-T7 are recorded by label count with no endpoints: the hips are diagonal and the jack positions are not dimensioned — a deliberate departure from the beam-endpoint rule, accepted because inventing ~20 more scaled dummy lines for short jacks would add guessed geometry, not read geometry; the detail sheets carry their shapes.
The left end prints fewer jack labels than the right end (no labels on the vertical jacks); counts are taken from the fully-labelled right end, doubled — flagged.
